svg.text: Inside DeepInfer's KV cache: one block and one state slot
Byte layout of the two device buffers that CacheEngine allocates · DeepSeek-V4.1 layer kinds · commit 9bd9cf2
gpu_blocks: uint8 [num_gpu_blocks, bytes_per_block] gpu_states: uint8 [num_state_slots, state_bytes]
What does one KV block hold? 128 tokens, for every layer that has a paged cache
Block #b is one row of gpu_blocks. Each layer owns a fixed byte range in every row, so one block id serves all layers.
gpu_blocks[b] = one row of bytes (layer ranges in layer order, each padded to 32 B)
Block 0 exists but is never used.
What does one state slot hold? A fixed area per running sequence, not paged
Slot s is one row of gpu_states. The sequence keeps it from start to end. Ring buffers overwrite old tokens.
gpu_states[state_id] = [ stored region | dropped region ] (StateBlock, cache_engine.py:221-241)
one ring per stored SWA layer
token at pos p → ring row p % 134
Doc: first 20 SWA layers are stored
Fixed size: no growth per token.
Main cache sizes use the HF loader default, FP4 with 288 B per entry (hugging_face/config.py:302-303). If config.json sets use_fp4_sparse_kv to false, an entry is 528 B
(MXFP8). The SWA ring always uses 528 B.
Byte widths in the two bars are not to scale. Which layer is C1, C2, sparse or SWA-only comes from the model config (attn_module_list), which is not in the repo.
Window 128 and the 20 stored layers are from doc/inference_deployment_qa.md:163,169,191. With DEEPINFER_PREFILL_STORE_EXTRA_STATE the rings are 128 tokens
longer (plus the YOCO keep tokens if truncation is on).
